# ZnCu₃(OD)₆Cl₂ on HRPT

Fit herbertsmithite, ZnCu₃(OD)₆Cl₂, a deuterated kagome antiferromagnet, to constant-wavelength
neutron powder data from HRPT at PSI, with a pseudo-Voigt profile and Bérar-Baldinozzi
asymmetry.

The project is the catalogue case `pd-neut-cwl_hs-hrpt`, the one the command line and the app's
Examples open.

<span style="color:#398648;background:#39864821;border-radius:3px;padding:0.1em 0.4em;font-size:0.85em"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="" width="14" height="14" style="height:0.85em;width:auto;vertical-align:-0.1em;margin-right:0.3em">Fitting</span> <span style="color:#96601d;background:#96601d21;border-radius:3px;padding:0.1em 0.4em;font-size:0.85em"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="" width="14" height="14" style="height:0.85em;width:auto;vertical-align:-0.1em;margin-right:0.3em">Single</span> <span style="color:#0084c7;background:#0084c721;border-radius:3px;padding:0.1em 0.4em;font-size:0.85em">pd</span> <span style="color:#0084c7;background:#0084c721;border-radius:3px;padding:0.1em 0.4em;font-size:0.85em">neut</span> <span style="color:#424242;background:#42424221;border-radius:3px;padding:0.1em 0.4em;font-size:0.85em">cwl</span> <span style="color:#0084c7;background:#0084c721;border-radius:3px;padding:0.1em 0.4em;font-size:0.85em">Bragg</span> <span style="color:#00796b;background:#00796b21;border-radius:3px;padding:0.1em 0.4em;font-size:0.85em"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="" width="14" height="14" style="height:0.85em;width:auto;vertical-align:-0.1em;margin-right:0.3em">Crystal structure</span>

```python
import easydiffraction as edi
```

## Load the project

```python
project_path = edi.download_data('pd-neut-cwl_hs-hrpt', destination='data')
project = edi.Project.load(project_path)
structure = project.structures['hs']
experiment = project.experiments['hrpt']
```

```text
Data 'pd-neut-cwl_hs-hrpt' is at data/pd-neut-cwl_hs-hrpt-dc870810b0b3/pd-neut-cwl_hs-hrpt
```

The project marks what its fit frees. The fit below frees it in stages, so start with all of it
fixed.

```python
for parameter in project.free_parameters:
    parameter.free = False
```

```python
project.display.pattern('hrpt')
```

## Perform the analysis

The fit follows diffraction-lib's four cycles for this case.

### Cell, scale and 2θ zero

The cell lengths, the scale and the zero shift put the peaks in place and at the right height.

```python
structure.cell.length_a.free = True
structure.cell.length_c.free = True
experiment.linked_structures['hs'].scale.free = True
experiment.instrument.calib_twotheta_offset.free = True
```

```python
project.display.parameters.free()
```

### Background

The estimated points are a starting point; fit them now that the peaks are in place.

```python
for point in experiment.background:
    point.intensity.free = True
```

```python
project.analysis.fit()
project.display.fit.results()
```

### Peak widths

The Gaussian widths and the mixing η₀, with the background staying free. diffraction-lib frees
the Lorentzian Y where this profile has η₀.

```python
experiment.peak.broad_gauss_u.free = True
experiment.peak.broad_gauss_v.free = True
experiment.peak.broad_gauss_w.free = True
experiment.peak.mixing_eta_0.free = True
```

```python
project.analysis.fit()
project.display.fit.results()
```

### Atom positions

The coordinates the symmetry leaves free: O and H in x and z, Cl in z.

```python
for site in structure.atom_sites:
    for coordinate in (site.fract_x, site.fract_y, site.fract_z):
        coordinate.free = not coordinate.symmetry_constrained
```

```python
project.analysis.fit()
project.display.fit.results()
```

```python
experiment.peak.asym_beba_a1.free = True
experiment.peak.asym_beba_b1.free = True
```
